brief: The AI trade assumes compute demand is nearly limitless and highly elastic. Compute demand equals the number of economically viable tasks LLMs can perform times compute per task, and the bull case leans on the Jevons paradox: falling token prices are assumed to always raise demand enough to offset them. But task demand may not be limitless. Growth requires models to keep improving and the task universe to keep expanding, neither guaranteed. AI labs need continued scaling to avoid being priced as mere inferencers, and training already consumes roughly 20-40% of tokens, so a scaling slowdown would hit demand materially. The deepest assumption is that intelligence itself is unbounded; researcher Francois Chollet argues intelligence has diminishing returns past an optimal point, and many problems are computationally irreducible and may never be economically tractable for LLMs. Forward P/Es on AI-related stocks have already slumped even as forward earnings and margins rose, but valuations still show nowhere near enough scepticism for the case where the demand assumption fails.
